anchors.sourceText: 2. Historical Background and Pre-Deep Learning Methods

pagePortrait.summary: text page with list x1; pageType:title-text, layout:text

anchors.sourceText: Computational linguistics is an interdisciplinary field concerned with the statistical or rule-based modeling of natural language from a computational perspective.
How can computers process and understand human language?
What are the limitations of traditional rule-based systems?
How has the paradigm shifted with the advent of neural networks?

pagePortrait.summary: grid page with grid:1x2 x1; pageType:grid-2, layout:grid, grid:1x2

anchors.sourceText: Relied heavily on hand-crafted grammar rules. Brittle and unable to scale to broad coverage of natural language.
Utilized probabilistic models (e.g., Hidden Markov Models). Better generalization but limited by feature engineering.

pagePortrait.summary: text page with list x1; pageType:title-text, layout:text

anchors.sourceText: Bengio et al. (2003): A Neural Probabilistic Language Model. Introduced distributed representations for words (word embeddings).
Mikolov et al. (2013): Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space (Word2Vec). Scaled up embedding generation.
Sutskever et al. (2014): Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks. Established the encoder-decoder architecture for translation.

pagePortrait.summary: text page with list x1; pageType:title-text, layout:text

anchors.sourceText: Vaswani et al. (2017): Attention Is All You Need. Replaced recurrent layers with self-attention mechanisms.
Devlin et al. (2018): BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding.
Brown et al. (2020): Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3). Demonstrated the power of massive scaling.

pagePortrait.summary: text page with list x1; pageType:title-text, layout:text

anchors.sourceText: Our research focuses on fine-tuning pre-trained transformer models for low-resource languages.
Select a multilingual base model (e.g., mBERT, XLM-R).
Compile a domain-specific corpus in the target language.
Apply continued pre-training using Masked Language Modeling (MLM).
Fine-tune on downstream tasks (NER, Sentiment Analysis).

pagePortrait.summary: text page with list x1; pageType:title-text, layout:text

anchors.sourceText: Data is the bottleneck for low-resource NLP. We utilized several strategies:
Web Scraping: Automated crawlers targeting local news websites and forums.
Crowdsourcing: Engaging native speakers for annotation and validation tasks.
Synthetic Data: Utilizing high-resource language models to generate parallel corpora via translation, followed by human filtering.

pagePortrait.summary: text page with list x1; pageType:title-text, layout:text

anchors.sourceText: The significant performance gains demonstrate the efficacy of continued pre-training on domain-specific, low-resource corpora.
Transfer learning mitigates the lack of massive annotated datasets.
However, the model still struggles with idiomatic expressions and code-switching, which are prevalent in the target language.

pagePortrait.summary: text page with list x1; pageType:title-text, layout:text

anchors.sourceText: Dataset Bias: Our web-scraped corpus heavily over-represents formal news text, potentially reducing performance on informal social media text.
Computational Cost: Fine-tuning large language models requires significant GPU resources, making deployment difficult in resource-constrained environments.
Evaluation Scope: The study is currently limited to two downstream tasks.

pagePortrait.summary: grid page with grid:1x2 x1; pageType:grid-2, layout:grid, grid:1x2

anchors.sourceText: Subsequent research will focus on addressing current limitations:
Compressing the fine-tuned model to run efficiently on mobile devices or edge servers.
Integrating acoustic and visual data to improve context understanding in spoken interactions.
